claims: A SSA Continuing Disability Review (CDR) is a periodic evaluation of the medical condition to determine if the person is still disabled and eligible for benefits.
SSA Continuing Disability Reviews occur every 6–18 months if improvement is expected.
SSA Continuing Disability Reviews occur every 3–7 years if improvement is not expected.
The SSA sends a letter and either the Form SSA-455 (Disability Update Report) or Form SSA-454 (Continuing Disability Review Report) during the CDR process.
Under the Medical Improvement Review Standard (MIRS), the SSA must determine if there has been medical improvement related to the ability to work.
Names of doctors, medical records from the last 12 months, prescriptions, and information on any work done are what to provide for a CDR.
If the forms are not returned within 30 days, benefits may be stopped.
If the SSA determines benefits should stop, the recipient has the right to appeal that decision.
